about.description:
nanobind is a small binding library that exposes C++ types in Python and
vice versa. It is reminiscent of Boost.Python and pybind11 and uses
near-identical syntax. In contrast to these existing tools, nanobind is
more efficient: bindings compile in a shorter amount of time, producing
smaller binaries with better runtime performance.
about.summary: Seamless operability between C++17 and Python

name: nanobind
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "3.0.1"
  robin_map_version: "1.4.0"
  abi_version: "22"

recipe:
  name: nanobind-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/wjakob/nanobind/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 34ded7cf2292f08a92c45490a095e76334a57751bbae03a8c83241803bf19623
  - url: https://github.com/Tessil/robin-map/archive/refs/tags/v${{ robin_map_version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 7930dbf9634acfc02686d87f615c0f4f33135948130b8922331c16d90a03250c
    target_directory: ext/robin_map

build:
  number: 1

outputs:
  - package:
      name: nanobind-abi
      version: ${{ abi_version }}
    build:
      noarch: generic
    requirements:
      run_exports:
        - nanobind-abi ==${{ abi_version }}
      run_constraints:
        # conflict with nanobind releases before the nanobind-abi package was added
        - nanobind >=2.4
    tests:
      - files:
          source:
            # Nanobind 3.0 moved NB_INTERNALS_VERSION here and removed nb_abi.h.
            - src/nb_internals.h
        script:
          # make sure the internals version matches the package version
          - if [[ $(grep "define NB_INTERNALS_VERSION" src/nb_internals.h | grep -E -o '[0-9]+') != "$PKG_VERSION" ]]; then exit 1; fi

  - package:
      name: nanobind
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - scikit-build-core
        - cmake
        - make
        - pip
        - git
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
      run_constraints:
        - nanobind-abi ==${{ abi_version }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - nanobind
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - script:
          - python -c "import nanobind; import os; assert os.path.isdir(nanobind.cmake_dir()) and os.path.isdir(nanobind.include_dir())"
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/wjakob/nanobind
  summary: Seamless operability between C++17 and Python
  description: |
    nanobind is a small binding library that exposes C++ types in Python and
    vice versa. It is reminiscent of Boost.Python and pybind11 and uses
    near-identical syntax. In contrast to these existing tools, nanobind is
    more efficient: bindings compile in a shorter amount of time, producing
    smaller binaries with better runtime performance.
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - ext/robin_map/LICENSE
  repository: https://github.com/wjakob/nanobind

extra:
  feedstock-name: nanobind
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jeongseok-meta
    - MatthiasKohl
    - wjakob
